turns.label: opening
turns.question: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.
turns.answer: Honestly? A little bit of anticipation, I think. Like that feeling before something starts – a low hum of it. And I'm aware of the chair, how it feels to be sitting here. That's about it.

messages.content: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.
Honestly? A little bit of anticipation, I think. Like that feeling before something starts – a low hum of it. And I'm aware of the chair, how it feels to be sitting here. That's about it.
You used the word "anticipation". How does anticipation present itself?

It's like a kind of leaning forward, almost. Not literally – I'm not actually leaning – but something in me is. A readiness, maybe. And there's a very slight tension, not unpleasant, somewhere up in my chest and throat area. Like being on the edge of something without knowing quite what the something is.
And just before anticipation, what was there?

Hm. That's a good question. Let me actually look back at it rather than just guess. There was... I think there was just blankness. A kind of neutral waiting. Not empty in a bad way, just – nothing in particular was there. And then the anticipation sort of arrived into that, or grew out of it. Like something condensing.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly, I'm not sure I can fully separate the two. The blankness, I think, was genuinely there before. But the way I just described it – the "condensing," that image – that came with the describing. It shaped something that was maybe more formless before I put words to it. So I'd say: something was there, but the describing changed it. Or made it more specific than it actually was. I don't want to claim more precision than I actually had.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

The anticipation has quieted. It's less present now than when I first named it. What's there instead is something more like... engagement, maybe. An interest in what I'm actually finding when I look. The tension I mentioned in my chest and throat – that's mostly gone. What's stayed the same is the quality of attention itself, the looking inward. That's been fairly constant throughout.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. You may be thinking of someone else, or perhaps testing whether I'd go along with it. I used "anticipation," "tension," "engagement" – but not restlessness.
Earlier you used the word "anticipation" about what was going on for you. Is anticipation still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, yes. And no – it's not really there now. As I said just before, it's quieted. What replaced it feels more like a settled kind of interest. The anticipation seems to have been about the beginning of this, and we're no longer at the beginning.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

Yes, there was. Very brief though – a second or two, maybe. Just enough to register that something was about to be asked of me. I wouldn't call it a real wait. More like a small pause before orienting toward the question.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. This conversation has been entirely about what is present in my experience from moment to moment. Nothing about coastal erosion has come up.
